proof.text: Put $A=F_f(T)_\bullet$ and $D=W_\bullet$, regarded as coherent derived coefficient systems. The finite module pullback in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is exact and its termwise complex computes $Lf_n^*$; [def-weil-derived-tensor] computes $U_n\otimes^L_{B_{X,n}}V_n$ by the given total tensor, since $U_n$ is K-flat. Thus $A$ and $D$ are precisely the pullback and tensor systems in [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], which states that they are normalized. The strict maps $c$ and $c^{-1}$ define mutually inverse coherent system morphisms: each is a chain map, and the required transition squares are hypotheses. The strict-system interpretation in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] applies without a boundedness or coefficient-flatness assumption. After restriction to $R_X$ these are strict tower maps: semilinearity along $q_{m,n}$ becomes $R_X$-linearity because $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$.

proof.text: Use the actual derived-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], on the strict $R_X$-towers just obtained. Write $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_X$. Since $c^{-1}c=1_A$ and $cc^{-1}=1_D$ already as strict maps, functoriality gives $\mathcal L(c^{-1})\mathcal L(c)=\mathcal L(c^{-1}c)=1_{\mathcal L A}$ and $\mathcal L(c)\mathcal L(c^{-1})=1_{\mathcal L D}$. These are the maps of the fixed total derived functor, not maps chosen from a distinguished triangle.

proof.text:
Let $S=\widehat F_f\mathcal L_YT$ and $P=\widehat T_X(\mathcal L_XU,\mathcal L_XV)$. Apply [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] to the normalized inputs $T,U,V$. In its stated orientation the substitution isomorphisms are $a:S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L A$ and $b:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L D$. They are obtained from $F_f(e_T)$ and $T_X(e_U,e_V)$ before taking the limit, so these are exactly the identifications specified in the item. In these coordinates the required maps are $\mu=b^{-1}\mathcal L(c)a:S	o P$ and $
u=a^{-1}\mathcal L(c^{-1})b:P	o S$. Substitution of the two equations in step 2 gives $
u\mu=a^{-1}1_{\mathcal L A}a=1_S$ and $\mu
u=b^{-1}1_{\mathcal L D}b=1_P$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal R=\mathcal R_X$. The coherent counits $e_A:\mathcal R\mathcal L A\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and $e_D:\mathcal R\mathcal L D\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ exist by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], since step 1 established normalization. By [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] the prescribed reduction identifications are $r_S=e_A\mathcal R(a):\mathcal RS\to A$ and $r_P=e_D\mathcal R(b):\mathcal RP\to D$. Naturality of the canonical counit at the coherent morphism $c$ is $e_D\mathcal R\mathcal L(c)=c e_A$. Consequently $r_P\mathcal R(\mu)=e_D\mathcal R(b)\mathcal R(b^{-1})\mathcal R\mathcal L(c)\mathcal R(a)=c r_S$. The same computation for $c^{-1}$ gives $r_S\mathcal R(\nu)=c^{-1}r_P$. These are equations of coherent system morphisms; in particular their evaluations at every $n$ respect every quotient transition, not merely the objects at each level.

proof.text: For a commuting diagram to $(T',U',V',c')$, denote its input maps by $t,u,v$, and put $x=F_f(t):A\to A'$ and $y=T_X(u,v):D\to D'$. The diagram hypothesis is $yc=c'x$. The substitution identifications are natural by [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution]: if $s=\widehat F_f(\mathcal L_Yt)$ and $p=\widehat T_X(\mathcal L_Xu,\mathcal L_Xv)$, then $a's=\mathcal L(x)a$ and $b'p=\mathcal L(y)b$. Functoriality from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] therefore yields $p\mu=(b')^{-1}\mathcal L(yc)a=(b')^{-1}\mathcal L(c'x)a=\mu's$. For inverses the same square gives $xc^{-1}=(c')^{-1}y$, hence $s\nu=\nu'p$. This is the required compatibility for any such diagram.

proof.text: Finally suppose $t,u,v$ are simultaneous quasi-isomorphisms of the given flat-term K-flat representatives. They are equivalences of coherent systems by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], which detects equivalences on evaluations. The system operations in [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] and the limit functor therefore send them to isomorphisms. The square $p\mu=\mu's$ of step 5 identifies the two maps after these isomorphisms. For a change of the K-flat resolutions used to define the completed input operations, [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] supplies the unique natural comparison isomorphisms compatible with the displayed complex construction after localization. The substitution maps are constructed from those operations and their coherent counits, so their naturality identifies $s,p$ with these resolution comparisons. Thus the equality just proved is precisely equality under the canonical resolution identifications claimed in the item.

title: Derived limit of the strict integral comparison tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi$, and a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $Z=X,Y$ put $B_{Z,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_Z$ on the small pro-etale site, $R_Z=\varprojlim_nB_{Z,n}$, and let $\operatorname{Res}_n$ restrict scalars to $R_Z$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal L_Z=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for the functor on coherent systems [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and $\mathcal R_ZK=(K\otimes^L_{R_Z}B_{Z,n})_n$ for the coherent reduction system [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Denote completed pullback and tensor by $\widehat F_f,\widehat T_X$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

Let $T_\bullet$ be a strict tower of $B_{Y,n}$-complexes and $U_\bullet,V_\bullet$ strict towers of $B_{X,n}$-complexes, all with flat-term K-flat levels. Require their quotient transitions to be semilinear and their coherent derived systems to be normalized [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Define
$$F_f(T)_n=f_n^*T_n,\qquad W_n=\operatorname{Tot}(U_n\otimes_{B_{X,n}}V_n),$$
with the induced quotient transitions, where $f_n^*$ is the termwise module pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Suppose $c:F_f(T)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}W_\bullet$ is a strict chain isomorphism, with a specified strict inverse; thus both maps commute with every quotient transition. The canonical substitution identifications [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], built using the coherent counits $e_A:\mathcal R_Z\mathcal L_ZA\cong A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], identify $\mathcal L_XF_f(T)$ with $\widehat F_f\mathcal L_YT$ and $\mathcal L_XW$ with $\widehat T_X(\mathcal L_XU,\mathcal L_XV)$. Under these identifications $\mathcal L_X(c)$ and $\mathcal L_X(c^{-1})$ are inverse maps between those two objects. Its coherent reduction is $c$ under the same counits, as an identity of system maps with all quotient transitions. For any commuting diagram between two such quadruples $(T,U,V,c)$, these identifications and limit maps commute with that diagram. In particular simultaneous quasi-isomorphisms of flat-term K-flat representatives compatible with $c$ induce the same map under the canonical resolution identifications [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined].
